article_manifest.title: Mali: 900 Tankers Under Escort - What Africa Corps Actually Does in Mali
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: 900 Tankers Under Escort - What Africa Corps Actually Does in Mali
article_manifest.summary: On September 14, 2026, more than 900 fuel tankers entered Bamako under military escort, the Malian government announced. The figure sounds like a victory: the capital got its fuel. But the very need to herd 900 tankers into a single protected convoy is not a story about victory -- it is a story about how vulnerable the ordinary roads have become, the same roads through which Mali imports 95% of its fuel.

article_manifest.summary: Kidal: Colonel Attaher Maïga, from the "red beret" to the command of the FAMa to consolidate the presence of the Malian State The truth of the weapons and the terrain prevailed over the opposing propaganda: Kidal is definitively and fully released, secured and reinstated in the bosom of the Republic of Mali . Colonel Attaher Maiga In the aftermath of this decisive step taken by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), it is a poignant testimony, full of assurance, authority and patriotism, delivered by Colonel Attaher A.

article_manifest.title: Mali: what changes the takeover of Kidal by the army?
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: que change la reprise de Kidal par l'armée?
article_manifest.summary: By retaking the strategic town of Kidal in northern Mali on Tuesday, the Malian army supported by the Russian Africa Corps paramilitaries achieved a highly symbolic success, almost six months after losing control to the Tuareg separatists. But it is a ghost town deserted by its inhabitants that the central Malian state has recovered without fighting, while Bamako struggles to control its territory in this vast desert country plagued by a jihadist insurgency and the independence claims of Tuareg groups.

article_manifest.summary: Bamako, 7 October 2026 – The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are resolutely continuing their missions to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko According to the information provided by the General Staff of the Armed Forces, several aero-terrestrial actions were carried out on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 in different sectors of the Eastern Theater, in particular in the Talhandak areas, north of Kidal and in the Tessalit region .

article_manifest.title: The Malian army recaptures the strategic city of Kidal from the Tuareg rebels.. article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso Orders Major Curriculum Overhaul

The government said the changes are intended to “decolonise” what students are taught as the new school year begins. Higher Education Minister Moumouni Zoungrana said the reform was carried out at the instruction of the prime minister and aimed to correct content inherited from the colonial period.

After four months of supervision combining military discipline and teaching civic values, a hundred supporters of the preacher Mohamad Ishaq Kindo reunited with their families on Sunday, October 4, 2026 .

article_manifest.summary: Recapture of the city of Kidal: THE INTREPID FAMAS CONSOLIDATE THEIR PRESENCE IN KIDAL AFTER A VAST AERO-TERRESTRIAL OPERATION They spoke of the city of Kidal on their media, as an impregnable city, inaccessible or even the indestructible strongholds of their terrorist acolytes. However, the warning had been raised by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and their Russian allies of Africa Corps, during the Battle of Anefif .

The ceremony took place in the presence of the Zone Commander, Colonel Ibrahim SAMASSA, representatives of the directors of services of the security forces as well as the Prefect of Gao, Benenan MOUNKORO, alongside several guests and personalities from the region.

In the nearby town of Gao, thousands of Kidal residents, such as teacher Almoustapha Maiga, found refuge .

For some Malians, the priority is to strengthen the security system. Others advocate for dialogue and the restoration of basic social services in order to consolidate this presence.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Junta forces retake strategic town of Kidal
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: Junta forces retake strategic town of Kidal
article_manifest.summary: Mali's army, supported by Russian paramilitary forces, has re-entered the northern town of Kidal, forcing the Tuareg separatists to withdraw from the strategic hold, in a symbolic boost for the country's military government and its Russian allies. The Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) said in a statement it had "decided to carry out a strategic and controlled withdrawal of its forces from the town of Kidal." It said the withdrawal took place without direct fighting.

article_manifest.title: Kidal: the Malian army regains control of the city
article_manifest.original_title: Kidal : l’armée malienne reprend le contrôle de la ville
article_manifest.summary: The Malian army regained control of Kidal, in northern Mali, on Tuesday, October 6. The Malian Armed Forces entered the city without resistance. This return comes more than five months after the capture of Kidal by the Azawad Liberation Front (Fla), allied to the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) Several security sources confirm this entry of the Fama into Kidal.

article_manifest.title: Mali’s army says it has taken Kidal from Tuareg rebels, with Russia’s help
article_manifest.original_title: Mali’s army says it has taken Kidal from Tuareg rebels, with Russia’s help
article_manifest.summary: Mali’s armed forces have entered the strategic northern city of Kidal, five months after separatist rebels seized it, following an air and ground campaign backed by Russia’s Africa Corps. In a statement carried by state television on Tuesday, Mali’s transitional government said troops had “consolidated their positions” in the city, “supported by their Russian partners”.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso Opens First Gold Refinery
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso Opens First Gold Refinery
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso has opened its first gold refinery as the West African country seeks to strengthen state control over the commercialisation of its mineral resources and reduce gold smuggling. The country is Africa’s third-largest gold producer, producing more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal in 2025, according to the World Gold Council. Authorities have struggled to regulate informal gold mining, a sector affected by smuggling and jihadist violence.
